cissp.lede: Use CISSP-specific study guidance to connect the eight exam domains to risk, governance, architecture, operations, and organizational decision-making.

status.label: How to use this hub
status.heading: Start with the study guide, then map the scope to your experience
status.body: Use the CISSP study guide to organize all eight domains. The domain guides build from governance and risk through asset protection, secure architecture, protected communications, identity and access management, assessment and testing, security operations, and software development security.

summary: CISSP covers security across an entire organization. Technical knowledge still matters, but candidates also need to connect controls to business objectives, legal duties, architecture, risk, operations, and program leadership.

The certification is aimed at experienced security practitioners, managers, architects, consultants, and senior technical professionals who need to reason across several security disciplines rather than stay inside one product or job function.

audience.heading: Who CISSP is built for
paragraphs: CISSP is designed for experienced professionals who design, manage, assess, or lead security work. That can include security managers and executives, but it also includes architects, engineers, consultants, auditors, and senior practitioners whose decisions affect more than one system.
The breadth is part of the challenge. A candidate may be deeply experienced in operations, networking, governance, or architecture and still need deliberate study in the other domains.
signals: You regularly connect technical findings to organizational risk.
You help choose, justify, or govern security controls.
You work across teams such as legal, privacy, software, networking, operations, and leadership.
You need to explain why a security decision is appropriate, not only how to configure it.

comparison.intro: Security+ provides a strong foundation for many CISSP topics. CISSP asks you to widen the frame around those topics.

entries.title: Controls and tools
entries.advanced: Evaluate whether the control fits business requirements, risk tolerance, architecture, policy, law, cost, and lifecycle obligations.
entries.foundation: Recognize the control or tool that best addresses a stated problem.

entries.title: Incident response
entries.advanced: Balance response priorities with governance, communications, legal considerations, business continuity, and lessons learned.
entries.foundation: Choose the correct response action, evidence source, or containment step.

entries.title: Architecture
entries.advanced: Select and defend architecture based on requirements, trust boundaries, system models, resilience, and organizational constraints.
entries.foundation: Identify secure design patterns and implementation choices.

entries.title: Risk
entries.advanced: Apply risk decisions across programs, suppliers, assets, data, compliance duties, and executive accountability.
entries.foundation: Understand risk concepts, treatment options, and common frameworks.

experience.heading: Experience and certification path
paragraphs: To earn the CISSP certification, a candidate generally needs five years of cumulative full-time work experience in at least two of the eight domains. A qualifying degree or an approved credential can waive up to one year, but the waivers do not stack.

Security+ is currently on ISC2's approved credential list for the one-year experience waiver. Passing the exam without the required experience can lead to Associate of ISC2 status while the candidate earns the remaining experience. ISC2 currently allows up to six years to complete that requirement.

Passing the exam is followed by the certification application and endorsement process. Certified members must also support the ISC2 Code of Ethics, pay the annual maintenance fee, and meet continuing professional education requirements.

maintenance.label: CPE requirement
maintenance.value: 120 credits during each three-year certification cycle

maintenance.label: Multiple ISC2 certifications
maintenance.value: One member AMF applies rather than a separate fee for every certification

steps.title: Start with the official outline

steps.title: Translate experience into the full scope

steps.body: Practice connecting security choices to business objectives, policy, risk, architecture, legal duties, and operational consequences.

steps.title: Review why alternatives are weaker
steps.body: A useful practice question should explain why a plausible option is not the best fit under the stated constraints.

steps.title: Plan beyond exam day
steps.body: Understand endorsement, experience documentation, CPE reporting, and the annual maintenance obligation before scheduling the exam.

ccna.name: CCNA
ccna.title: CCNA 200-301 Study Resources
ccna.lede: Practice with randomized v2.0 questions, work through all five domain guides, review Cisco IOS verification commands, and reinforce subnetting and protocol knowledge. Check the exam-version guidance below so your preparation matches your test date.

status.label: Which blueprint should you study?
status.heading: Use v1.1 through February 2, 2027 and v2.0 starting February 3, 2027
status.body: If your exam is scheduled by February 2, prepare against the active v1.1 blueprint. For an exam on or after February 3, use the published v2.0 scope. The technical core overlaps heavily, so work on addressing, switching, routing, services, security, automation, and troubleshooting remains useful across the transition.

summary: CCNA measures whether a candidate can understand, configure, verify, and troubleshoot a small to medium network. Addressing, switching, routing, security, services, and network operations are connected through practical decisions rather than treated as isolated definitions.

The current 200-301 v1.1 exam remains available through February 2, 2027. Cisco's published v2.0 blueprint takes effect February 3, 2027 and consolidates the exam into five domains with heavier emphasis on troubleshooting, practical configuration, security, and AI-assisted network operations.

transition.heading: What carries forward to CCNA v2.0
paragraphs: Candidates planning to test by February 2, 2027 should continue using the current v1.1 blueprint. Cisco has said the refresh keeps the technical core, so current study in subnetting, switching, routing, services, security, and automation still carries forward.

For v2.0, put extra attention on practical verification and troubleshooting. Be ready to connect configuration intent with interface state, switching and routing tables, neighbor relationships, logs, packet evidence, security controls, and AI-assisted network operations.

facts.label: Refresh emphasis
facts.value: Practical skills, troubleshooting, security, and AI

audience.heading: Who CCNA is built for
paragraphs: CCNA is aimed at people entering or advancing in network engineering, network administration, infrastructure support, and related security or cloud roles. It is also useful for experienced support professionals who need stronger routing, switching, and troubleshooting depth.

There is no formal certification prerequisite. The practical challenge is being able to move between concepts, command output, configuration intent, and fault evidence without losing track of how traffic should flow.
audience.signalHeading: Signals that CCNA may fit your next step
signals: You understand basic networking and want to configure and verify it rather than only describe it.
You need stronger routing, switching, wireless, or infrastructure troubleshooting skills.
You work with Cisco IOS or expect to support Cisco-based environments.
You want a networking foundation that can lead toward security, cloud, automation, or professional-level Cisco study.

comparison.heading: What changes after Network+
comparison.intro: Network+ provides broad vendor-neutral coverage. CCNA expects more configuration fluency, output interpretation, and device-level verification.

entries.title: Addressing and subnetting
entries.foundation: Calculate subnets, host ranges, masks, and addressing requirements.
entries.advanced: Apply IPv4 and IPv6 addressing to interfaces, routing decisions, VLAN designs, and troubleshooting evidence.

entries.title: Switching
entries.foundation: Explain VLANs, trunks, spanning tree, link aggregation, and common Layer 2 faults.
entries.advanced: Interpret and verify Cisco switch configuration, trunk state, VLAN membership, spanning-tree roles, and EtherChannel operation.

entries.title: Routing
entries.foundation: Understand route selection, static and dynamic routing, and common path problems.
entries.advanced: Read routing tables, select the most specific route, configure IPv4 and IPv6 paths, and verify OSPF and static routing behavior.

entries.title: Troubleshooting
entries.foundation: Use a structured method and choose appropriate commands, tools, and evidence.
entries.advanced: Combine interface state, configuration, tables, logs, and command output to isolate the fault and choose the next verification step.

entries.title: Automation and management
entries.foundation: Recognize APIs, configuration management, software-defined networking, and automation concepts.
entries.advanced: Understand how controllers, APIs, data formats, automation tools, and AI-assisted operations fit into modern Cisco network management.

scope.heading: Five CCNA v2.0 domains
scope.intro: Cisco has published the v2.0 blueprint for exams beginning February 3, 2027. Candidates testing through February 2, 2027 should continue using the active v1.1 blueprint for their exam-specific preparation.

domains.name: Network Infrastructure and Connectivity
domains.focus: Interface and cabling faults, virtualization, IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, wireless principles, wired and wireless client connectivity, and Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol version 4 (DHCPv4) troubleshooting on IOS devices.

domains.name: Switching and Network Access
domains.focus: Layer 2 and Layer 3 interfaces, 802.1Q trunks, Link Aggregation Control Protocol (LACP) EtherChannel, switch virtual interfaces (SVIs), edge-port configuration, Cisco Discovery Protocol (CDP) and Link Layer Discovery Protocol (LLDP) validation, troubleshooting output, and Rapid Per-VLAN Spanning Tree Plus (Rapid PVST+).

domains.name: IP Routing
domains.focus: Routing-table interpretation, IPv4 and IPv6 static routing, single-area Open Shortest Path First (OSPFv2 and OSPFv3), and operational status of first-hop redundancy protocols.

domains.name: Network Services and Security
domains.focus: AAA management access, secure file transfer, NAT and PAT, DNS troubleshooting, IPsec VPN concepts, IPv4 access control lists, and Layer 2 protections such as DHCP snooping, Dynamic ARP Inspection, RA guard, and port security.

domains.name: AI, and Network Operations and Management
domains.focus: Agentic AI, prompt selection for generative AI-assisted operations, device-, cloud-, controller-, automation-, and infrastructure-as-code management, Simple Network Management Protocol (SNMP), Ansible command execution, and syslog interpretation.

experience.heading: One exam, then an active certification cycle
paragraphs: CCNA has no formal degree or prior-certification prerequisite. Earning it requires passing the current 200-301 exam version available on the candidate’s test date.

Most Cisco certifications, including CCNA, remain active for three years. Associate-level recertification can be completed through qualifying exams, 30 Continuing Education credits, or another current option listed in Cisco’s recertification policy.
Because the exam version changes in February 2027, candidates should verify the active blueprint before scheduling and make sure their preparation materials match their intended test date.

preparation.heading: Build command fluency around the network model

steps.title: Lock down the fundamentals
steps.body: Be comfortable with subnetting, Ethernet, VLANs, trunks, routing logic, wireless basics, and common services before adding command memorization.

steps.title: Use a lab from the beginning
steps.body: Practice on Packet Tracer, Cisco Modeling Labs, or suitable equipment so configuration and verification commands are connected to visible network behavior.

steps.title: Read output before changing configuration
steps.body: Learn what normal interface, VLAN, spanning-tree, neighbor, and routing output looks like. Troubleshooting improves when evidence comes before guesses.

steps.title: Practice the next best command
steps.body: Do not stop at identifying the likely fault. Decide which command or observation would confirm it with the least unnecessary change.

steps.title: Track the exam version
steps.body: Use v1.1 material for a test scheduled by February 2, 2027. Use the published v2.0 scope for testing on or after February 3, 2027.
